title: Debug

blocks.surrounding_prose: Section header: '## 9. Debug — *(as needed)*'. Immediately after the fence: 'Runs the `debugger` agent under `systematic-debugging` — root-cause-first, one falsifiable hypothesis at a time, a 3-strike rule, and a persistent debug file that survives a context reset.' Then: 'A resolved session feeds two separate knowledge stores, and only one of them is unconditional:' which leads into the second fenced block.

blocks.verbatim_text:
Before you close this out, walk the archive step. Every resolved session — not just the
interesting ones — appends its entry to docs/state/debug/knowledge-base.md, the symptom-matched
case log that gets read at the start of every future investigation, committed alongside the
resolved session file. That one is unconditional.

Then apply the durable-pattern check: would this root cause bite in a different file or
context — a project-wide habit, a systemic misuse of a library, a missing convention — rather
than just recurring in this exact spot? Only if yes, also cross-post a pitfall entry to learn's
ledger. Most resolved bugs are ordinary and do not qualify; do not promote one just because the
debugging was hard.

The two stores are deliberately not the same thing: the knowledge base is a case log matched by
symptom keywords and written for every bug, while learn's ledger is a curated cross-session
insight store. Do not fold either into the other. Tell me which of the two you wrote.
blocks.surrounding_prose: This is a follow-up prompt the operator pastes after the debug session resolves, per the preceding sentence 'A resolved session feeds two separate knowledge stores, and only one of them is unconditional:'. It does not invoke a skill/agent/command by name; it instructs writing to docs/state/debug/knowledge-base.md unconditionally, and conditionally (only if the root cause is a durable/project-wide pattern) cross-posting to 'learn's ledger' (referring to a separate learn-related asset elsewhere in the guide, not invoked here by name). Followed by '---' section divider.
